breakfast.name: Dan Bing (Egg Crepe)
instructions: Pour thin batter on griddle
Crack egg on top, spread
Add scallion, roll up
Cut into pieces, serve with soy paste
breakfast.description: Thin egg crepe roll — Taiwan's most popular breakfast.

breakfast.name: Doujiang and Youtiao (Soy Milk and Cruller)
instructions: Serve hot soy milk (sweet or salty)
Dip fried cruller into soy milk
breakfast.description: Classic Taiwanese breakfast — soy milk with fried dough.

breakfast.name: Dan Bing (Egg Crepe Roll)
ingredients: Thin rice-flour or wheat crepe (pre-made or from batter)
instructions: Dan bing is one of the most popular Taiwanese breakfast items
A thin crepe is laid on a griddle
An egg is poured over it and the crepe is flipped to cook the egg
Rolled up into a cylinder
The egg-crepe combination is simple but deeply satisfying
Eaten with soy sauce or sweet chilli
The breakfast shop (zaocan dian) is the Taiwanese breakfast institution -- opens before 6am and often closes by 10am
breakfast.description: Taiwanese egg crepe roll -- a thin crepe with a beaten egg poured and cooked on top, rolled into a cylinder. Green onion and sesame oil inside. The breakfast shop (zaocan dian) opens before 6am and closes by 10am; dan bing is one of the staples. Eaten with soy sauce.

breakfast.name: Shao Bing (Sesame Flatbread)
ingredients: Flour dough (layered with oil -- puff-pastry technique)
Optional filling: you tiao (fried dough) for shao bing you tiao
instructions: Shao bing is the sesame flatbread baked in a clay oven
Layered dough that creates a flaky interior
Coated in sesame seeds and baked until crispy
Eaten alone or as a sandwich with you tiao (fried dough stick) inside
Shao bing you tiao: the Taiwanese breakfast sandwich -- shao bing split and you tiao placed inside
Northern Chinese origin brought to Taiwan with the Nationalist migration (1949)
breakfast.description: Taiwanese sesame flatbread -- layered dough baked until crispy with a flaky interior, coated in sesame seeds. Northern Chinese origin brought to Taiwan by Nationalist migrants (1949). Eaten with you tiao (fried dough stick) inside as shao bing you tiao.

lunch.name: Beef Noodle Soup
instructions: Simmer bones for broth
Braise beef shank with soy, doubanjiang, spices 2 hours
Cook noodles
Serve in broth with sliced beef
Top with bok choy and green onion
lunch.description: Taiwan's national dish — rich, spicy braised beef over noodles.

lunch.name: Lu Rou Fan (Braised Pork Rice)
instructions: Fry shallots until crispy
Braise pork belly with soy, wine, five spice, sugar
Add fried shallots and eggs
Simmer 45 min
Serve over rice
lunch.description: Fragrant braised pork belly over steamed rice.

lunch.name: Lu Rou Fan (Braised Pork Rice)
ingredients: Pork belly (with skin, cut into small pieces)
Soy sauce, dark soy sauce, rice wine
instructions: Lu rou fan is the Taiwanese soul food -- braised pork over rice
Pork belly braised for 1-2 hours in soy sauce, rice wine, and five spice
The skin and fat become gelatinous -- they melt into the braising liquid
Fried shallots are the essential addition
The braising liquid reduces to a thick, fragrant sauce
A soy-braised egg (lu dan) is standard alongside
Every Taiwanese restaurant and home cook has their version
lunch.description: Taiwanese braised pork rice -- pork belly with skin braised for 1-2 hours in soy sauce, rice wine, five spice, and fried shallots until the fat is gelatinous and the liquid thick. Served over rice with a soy-braised egg. The Taiwanese soul food. Every restaurant and home cook has their version.

lunch.name: Oyster Vermicelli (O-A-Mi-Suah)
ingredients: Sweet potato starch noodles (very thin -- misua or vermicelli)
Thick starchy broth (sweet potato starch thickened)
instructions: Oyster vermicelli is a classic Taiwanese street food
The broth: thickened with sweet potato starch until silky and thick
Oysters and thin starch noodles in the thickened broth
The basil and ginger cut the brininess of the oysters
Eaten at Taiwanese night markets
The starchy thick broth is a distinctly Taiwanese texture preference
lunch.description: Taiwanese oyster noodle soup -- small fresh oysters and thin sweet potato starch noodles in a thick starchy broth (sweet potato starch: a distinctly Taiwanese texture). Basil and ginger cut the oyster brininess. Classic night market food.

lunch.name: Gua Bao (Taiwanese Pork Bun)
ingredients: Steamed folded bun (lotus leaf bun -- oval, folded)
Braised pork belly (same as lu rou fan: soy-braised until soft)
Peanut powder (ground roasted peanuts with sugar)
instructions: Gua bao is the Taiwanese steamed pork bun -- internationally known as a bao
The bun: a steamed folded mantou (the lotus leaf shape -- folded over the filling)
Stuffed with braised pork belly, pickled mustard greens, peanut powder, and coriander
The balance: soft braised pork + sour pickled greens + sweet-nutty peanut powder
The pickled mustard greens are the essential counterpart to the fatty pork
Globally famous as bao or Taiwanese burger -- popularized internationally in the 2010s
lunch.description: Taiwanese steamed pork bun -- a folded lotus-leaf steamed bun stuffed with braised pork belly, pickled mustard greens (suan cai), ground peanut powder (sweet), and coriander. The sour greens and sweet peanut powder balance the fatty pork. Globally famous as a bao.

dinner.name: San Bei Ji (Three Cup Chicken)
instructions: Sauté garlic, ginger in sesame oil
Add chicken, brown
Add equal parts soy sauce, sesame oil, rice wine
Simmer until sauce reduces and glazes
Toss with basil leaves
dinner.description: Three-cup chicken — named for its sauce ratio.

dinner.name: Gua Bao (Pork Belly Buns)
instructions: Braise pork belly in soy, sugar, spices 2 hours
Steam bao buns
Fill with sliced pork, greens, cilantro, peanuts
dinner.description: Pillowy steamed buns with braised pork belly — Taiwan's icon.

dinner.name: Three Cup Chicken (San Bei Ji)
ingredients: One cup soy sauce, one cup sesame oil, one cup rice wine (the three cups)
Fresh basil (a large amount -- added at the very end)
instructions: San bei ji (three cup chicken) is one of Taiwan's most beloved dishes
The three cups: one of soy sauce, one of sesame oil, one of rice wine (Taiwan Shaoxing or Michiu)
The ratio gives it a rich, glossy, intensely flavored sauce
Chicken is pan-fried until the skin is golden
Then the three-cup sauce is added and reduced around the chicken
Garlic and ginger are fried whole in the sesame oil first
Fresh basil is added in a large amount at the very end -- it wilts and releases its oils
The basil is the defining element
dinner.description: Taiwanese three cup chicken -- chicken pieces braised in equal parts soy sauce, sesame oil, and rice wine (the three cups), with garlic and ginger, reduced to a glossy intense sauce. A large amount of fresh basil stirred in at the end: the defining element. San bei ji is one of Taiwan's most beloved dishes.

dinner.name: Niu Rou Mian (Beef Noodle Soup)
ingredients: Fresh or dry noodles (flat wheat noodles)
Chilli oil, garlic chilli paste (for condiment)
instructions: Niu rou mian is the Taiwanese national dish -- beef noodle soup
An annual competition in Taipei determines the best beef noodle soup in Taiwan
The broth: a long-cooked beef bone broth flavored with soy sauce, doubanjiang (spicy bean paste), and warm spices
The beef shank braised until it falls apart
Served over thick wheat noodles in the rich broth
This dish came to Taiwan with the Nationalist migration from mainland China (1949)
The Sichuan immigrants brought their spicy doubanjiang -- combined with the Taiwanese braising tradition
The result is distinctly Taiwanese: spicy-savory-soy-braised
dinner.description: Taiwanese beef noodle soup -- beef shank braised in a soy-doubanjiang broth (spicy fermented broad bean paste) with star anise and Sichuan pepper, served over thick wheat noodles. Brought by Nationalist migrants in 1949. An annual competition in Taipei crowns the best version. Distinctly Taiwanese: spicy-soy-braised.

dinner.name: Scallion Pancakes (Cong You Bing)
ingredients: All-purpose flour, hot water (the hot water creates a tender dough)
instructions: Cong you bing is the Taiwanese (and Chinese) scallion pancake -- a street food staple
The dough is rolled, spread with sesame oil and scallions, then rolled up like a Swiss roll, then rolled flat again
This creates layers -- like a rough puff pastry
When fried, the layers separate and become crispy-flaky
The scallion and sesame oil fragrance is released
Eaten as a snack or breakfast -- with egg fried on top in Taiwan
dinner.description: Taiwanese scallion pancake -- dough rolled with sesame oil and spring onions, rolled into a cylinder, then rolled flat (creating layers), pan-fried until the layers separate and crisp. The flaky-crispy-scallion result. A street food staple eaten at breakfast shops and night markets.

snacks.name: Xiao Long Bao (Soup Dumplings)
instructions: Make thin wrappers
Mix pork with diced aspic
Pleat 18+ folds per dumpling
Steam 8 min
Dip in vinegar-ginger, bite hole, sip soup first
snacks.description: Soup dumplings — hot broth burst inside each one.

snacks.name: Stinky Tofu (Chou Doufu)
ingredients: Firm tofu (fermented in a brine of vegetables and meat for weeks -- the fermentation creates the smell)
instructions: Stinky tofu is the Taiwanese night market smell -- you find the stall by smell alone
Tofu fermented in a brine of vegetables, meat, and other aromatics for weeks to months
The fermentation creates a pungent, sulfurous smell
Deep-fried until the outside is crispy
The inside is soft and creamy -- the smell is the exterior experience
Eaten with pickled cabbage and chilli sauce
The smell is much stronger than the taste
A test of adventurous eating at every Taiwanese night market
snacks.description: Taiwanese fermented deep-fried tofu -- tofu fermented in a brine for weeks until pungently aromatic, deep-fried until crispy outside and soft inside. The smell leads you to the stall before you see it. Eaten with pickled cabbage and chilli sauce. The taste is milder than the smell suggests. Night market essential.

snacks.name: Pineapple Cake (Feng Li Su)
ingredients: Shortbread pastry (butter, flour, egg, sugar, salt)
Pineapple jam filling (pineapple cooked down with sugar -- or: winter melon jam is the traditional filling)
instructions: Feng li su (pineapple cake) is Taiwan's most famous souvenir gift food
A crumbly buttery shortbread shell
Filled with pineapple jam -- though traditionally the filling was winter melon jam (since pineapple was expensive)
Shaped into small rectangular blocks
The name means pineapple in Taiwanese (Hokkien): ong lai -- also means "prosperity comes"
The wordplay (prosperity comes) makes pineapple cake an auspicious gift
Bought by tourists and gifted by Taiwanese returning home
snacks.description: Taiwanese souvenir pastry -- crumbly buttery shortbread shell filled with pineapple jam (originally winter melon: pineapple was expensive). In Taiwanese Hokkien, pineapple (ong lai) sounds like "prosperity comes" -- making pineapple cake an auspicious gift. Taiwan's most famous souvenir food.

snacks.name: Bubble Tea (Zhen Zhu Nai Cha)
ingredients: Tapioca pearls (brown sugar coated -- cooked until chewy)
instructions: Bubble tea was invented in Taiwan -- at two competing cafes, both claiming credit
The Chun Shui Tang tearoom in Taichung (Lin Hsiu-Hui, 1988) and Hanlin Tea Room in Tainan are both credited
The tapioca pearl: made from cassava starch, cooked until chewy, often coated in brown sugar syrup
The tea is shaken with ice -- the bubbles are from the shaking, not the pearls
The fat straw is necessary for the pearls
Now a global beverage category -- Taiwan bubble tea chains (Tiger Sugar, Gong Cha, 50 Lan) are worldwide
snacks.description: Taiwanese invented drink -- strong tea shaken with milk and ice, served over chewy tapioca pearls (zhen zhu: pearl). Invented in Taiwan in 1988 (Taichung and Tainan both claim credit). The bubbles are from shaking, not the pearls. Now a global beverage category with worldwide Taiwanese chains.

desserts.name: Pineapple Cake
ingredients: Butter pastry: flour, butter, egg, sugar
instructions: Cook pineapple filling until thick
Make butter pastry dough
Fill molds with pastry and jam
Bake at 170°C 25-30 min
desserts.description: Buttery pastry with pineapple jam — Taiwan's most famous souvenir.

desserts.name: Taro Ball Dessert (Yü Yuan)
ingredients: Sweet potato (cooked and mashed -- for orange balls)
Sweet broth or shaved ice (to serve in)
instructions: Yü yuan are the Taiwanese taro and sweet potato starch balls
Two colors: purple (taro) and orange (sweet potato)
The balls are chewy and slightly sweet
Served either in warm sweet broth (tong yuan style) or over shaved ice
The specialty of Jiufen, the mountain town above Taipei -- the taro ball shops of Jiufen are famous
The Jiufen scenery inspired the setting of Spirited Away (disputed but a popular claim)
desserts.description: Taiwanese taro and sweet potato starch balls -- purple taro and orange sweet potato balls, chewy and slightly sweet, served in warm sweet broth or over shaved ice. The specialty of Jiufen (the mountain town above Taipei whose taro ball shops are iconic). The Jiufen hillside is associated with the Spirited Away aesthetic.

desserts.name: Mochi (Tang Yuan Style)
ingredients: Brown sugar syrup (for the black sugar version)
instructions: Taiwanese mochi differs from Japanese mochi -- softer and more chewy
Made from glutinous rice flour, shaped by hand
Filled with peanut paste or black sesame paste
Coated in peanut powder or shredded coconut
The Hualien region (eastern Taiwan) is famous for its mochi -- bought as a souvenir
The Hualien mochi: a gift from the east coast
desserts.description: Taiwanese glutinous rice cake -- softer and chewier than Japanese mochi, filled with peanut or sesame paste, coated in peanut powder. Hualien (eastern Taiwan) is the mochi region; Hualien mochi is a classic souvenir from the east coast.

drinks.name: Bubble Tea (Boba)
instructions: Cook tapioca pearls until chewy
Brew strong tea, sweeten
Add milk and ice
Add pearls, shake or stir
drinks.description: Taiwan's gift to the world — tea with chewy tapioca pearls.

drinks.name: Aiyu Jelly Drink
instructions: Squeeze aiyu seeds in water until jelly forms
Chill until set
Serve cubed with lime juice and sugar
drinks.description: Jiggly fig seed jelly in lime syrup — refreshing Taiwanese summer drink.

drinks.name: Soy Milk (Dou Jiang)
ingredients: Dried soybeans (soaked overnight, blended, then sieved)
Salt or you tiao (for the savory version)
instructions: Dou jiang (soy milk) is the Taiwanese breakfast drink -- every zaocan dian sells it
Fresh soy milk tastes completely different from packaged soy milk
Sweet version: sweetened and drunk hot or cold
Savory version: a small amount of salt, vinegar, chilli oil, and you tiao broken in -- the broth-like soy milk
The hot savory soy milk with you tiao is the northern Chinese breakfast that came to Taiwan with the 1949 migration
drinks.description: Taiwanese fresh soy milk -- dou jiang, soybeans soaked and blended then strained. Two versions: sweet (hot or cold) and savory (salted with vinegar, chilli oil, and broken you tiao dough stick). Northern Chinese breakfast brought to Taiwan in 1949. Fresh tastes completely different from packaged.
